To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the response to loading in both trabecal and cortical bone is not impaired by short term treatment with risedonate, even over an extremely wide dose range, and (ii) anti-resorptive treatment and mechanical loading can therefore exert independent beneficial effects in osteoporosis.
the response to mechanical bone loading in both trabecaular and cortical bone is not impaired by short term treatment with risedonate, even over an 1000-fold range of doses.
the response to mechanical stimulation in both trabecu-lar and cortical bone in young mice is not impaired by short term treatment with rised-ronate, even at a 1000 fold dose range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of action and the clinical efficacy of bisphosphonates in the treatment of osteoporosis.
the effects of bisphosphonates on bone cells and on the skeleton in vitro, in vivo and in patients.
the development of novel, more efficient and less toxic drugs for the treatment of bone disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of anti‐resorptive therapy with non‐invasive dynamic mechanical loading has a positive additive effect on bone structure in mice, and that this effect was not impaired by the treatment with risedonate over a 100‐fold dose range.
the response to mechanical stimulation of both trabecular bone and cortical bone is not impaired by short term treatment with risedronic acid.
the response of the skeleton to mechanical loading is not impaired by short term treatment with risedronic acid even over a 1,000-fold dose range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of anti‐resorptive therapy with dynamic loading does not impair the response of bone to mechanical loading.
mechanical loading is a powerful anabolic stimulus in the skeleton, which is not impaired by the administration of a bisphosphonate.
risedronate does NOT reduce the mechanical loading-related increases of cortical and trabeculae bone mass in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mechanical loading and risedronate can exert independent effects on bone structure.
mechanical loading and bisphosphonate therapy can be combined without any negative effects.
the response to mechanical load in both trabeculae and cortical bone in female mice is not impaired by treatment with a bisphosphonate, even over an extremely wide dose range.
